newsitem.title: UK: Few takers on Thanksgiving day in Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Few takers on Thanksgiving day in Brady market.

text.p: There was hardly a nibble in the emerging debt market on Thursday as most traders geared up to celebrate Thanksgiving Day, with trading finishing a midday.
Traders said the market will be effectively shut for most houses until next week.
"On the Latins, I can seven prices on eight screens and two of them are mine. To all intents and purposes the market is closed," one European bank trader said.
He added he was only in the office in the unlikely event some of his clients might want to trade.
About the only activity was in Russian MinFins, which were firmer.
Traders continue to see chances of a minor rally before the end of the year as some of the cash from recent profit-taking returns.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell suggested investors should switch out of Brazil EI bonds and into Argentine FRB.

"Hopes that Brazil will be buying back its external debt and bonds next year have receded...far from trying to reduce its debt, Brazil likely will be having to increase its sovereign borrowings, giving the markets piles of alternatives to EIs," it said in a strategy report.
In contrast, Argentina's room for manoeuvre is expanding and it could see four percent growth next year without exposing its exchange rate regime to any risks.
"We are not suggesting EIs necessarily will fall, simply that FRBs will do better. Put another way: candy is dandy, but liquor is quicker," it said.
